claim: Models optimized for structure-dependent PTM prediction may not generalize well to PTMs in highly disordered protein contexts.

conditions: when the model relies on structural features from AlphaFold

claim: A string s in the AQCE* problem family does not in general determine a unique quantum circuit; the same string can refer to different circuits depending on the AQCE* class to which it is considered a member.
falsifier: Take a string s that is a valid member of two different AQCE* classes and demonstrate that the described circuits differ in gate composition or structure.

conditions: the string s is considered as a member of different AQCE* classes with different basis gate sets
exclusions: limited to the AQCE* problem family as defined

title: AQCE* problem family–non-uniqueness of circuit interpretation theorem

claim: Problems in class P exhibit low and deterministic entropy values, while problems in class NP display higher and more varied entropy profiles, reflecting their inherent complexity and nondeterministic nature.
falsifier: Entropy profiles can be computed for other P and NP problems using the same entropy definition to test whether the observed pattern holds.

conditions: based on empirical analysis of selected problems including SAT and protein-DNA complex problem
exclusions: limited to the sampled problems and reported experimental conditions

title: Problem class–entropy profile of principle

claim: A general separability instance for a bipartite quantum state can be reduced to a separability instance with a fixed partial trace condition by embedding into a larger Hilbert space, preserving separability.
falsifier: One can test by implementing the reduction on random instances and verifying the separability equivalence.

conditions: Construct ρ' ∈ D(C^2 ⊗ C^M ⊗ C^N) such that Tr_{A'}(ρ') = I/N
ρ separable iff ρ' separable across A'/B split
